system.name: Tai Chi
system.one_liner: a hardware-software co-designed scheduler that uses SmartNIC-accelerated hybrid virtualization to coordinate control-plane tasks and data-plane services

components.name: LC task
components.role: latency-critical application task, shown per deployment model

components.name: BE task
components.role: best-effort/batch task scheduled alongside the LC task for CPU utilization

components.name: Custom scheduler
components.role: balances LC vs BE task scheduling on bare-metal

components.name: DPDK or SPDK
components.role: user-space I/O framework bypassing the kernel to reach NICs directly

components.name: NICs
components.role: physical network interface cards, the common endpoint of the I/O path in all three panels

components.name: VM 0
components.role: a tenant VM running LC/BE tasks and a NIC driver, shown in panels (b) and (c)

components.name: VM 1

components.name: NIC driver

components.name: Host
components.role: hypervisor host machine running QEMU/KVM, shown in panels (b) and (c)

components.name: vNIC
components.role: QEMU-emulated virtual NIC exposed to each VM (panel b)

components.name: QEMU and KVM
components.role: virtualization stack co-located with DPDK to accelerate I/O for VMs

components.name: SmartNIC
components.role: panel (c): compact PCIe device with general-purpose cores and programmable I/O acceleration hardware

components.name: CP tasks
components.role: control-plane tasks managing device operations, coordinating with QEMU on the host (panel c)

components.name: DP services
components.role: data-plane services statically reserving most SmartNIC cores for latency-sensitive I/O processing (panel c)

components.name: Core
components.role: general-purpose SmartNIC cores running CP tasks and DP services

components.name: eNIC

components.name: CSP

content.key_idea: Moving from bare-metal to VM-with-vNIC to VM-with-SmartNIC deployments progressively separates latency-critical I/O from control-plane device management, culminating in a SmartNIC that runs control-plane (CP) tasks and data-plane (DP) services on shared cores while a programmable accelerator exposes per-VM emulated NICs.
content.reading_order: Left to right across three increasingly complex panels (a, b, c); within panel (c), blue circled numbers trace the data-plane I/O path and red circled numbers trace the control-plane VM-creation path.

summary: Tai Chi is a hardware-software co-designed scheduler that uses SmartNIC-accelerated hybrid virtualization to coordinate latency-sensitive control-plane (CP) tasks and data-plane (DP) services on the same cores. Figure 1 is a background comparison of three I/O-acceleration deployment models, drawn as three side-by-side box diagrams of increasing complexity: (a) bare-metal, where an LC/BE task pair reaches NICs through a custom scheduler and DPDK/SPDK; (b) VMs with virtual NICs, where each VM's NIC driver reaches a host-side vNIC, QEMU/KVM, and DPDK/SPDK; and (c) VMs with SmartNICs, where a SmartNIC hosts CP tasks and DP services on shared cores plus a programmable I/O accelerator exposing per-VM eNICs. Blue circled numbers trace the data-plane I/O path from eNIC to DP services to the physical NICs; red circled numbers trace the control-plane VM-creation path from the CSP through CP tasks, DP-services coordination, and a QEMU notification.
